findings.title: A reused container id builds a second AuraMasterAnchor<id> frame set and leaks the old one when destroyed out of combat
findings.evidence: Only instances parked under CM.MustDefer() are revived. Out of combat, CM.Sync calls inst:Destroy() and drops the instance, and the next build calls NS.Container.New(id), which creates a new anchor/engine/blocker/outline/handle/preview pool and overwrites _G.AuraMasterAnchor<id>. Ids come back on a profile switch between profiles with different container counts, on reset (ResetProfile rewinds nextContainerId) and on copy. tests/test_containermanager.lua:488/:510 cover only the deferred half.
findings.remediation: C-01: keep destroyed instances in a dormant[id] table (CM.Sync non-deferred branch: Destroy then dormant[id]=inst; destroyParked moves to dormant). In follow(), add a dormant branch that sets staleData=true and calls revive(id, d, hold); CM.Announce already queues the apply. Add Container:Revive() only if re-Show is needed. Correct the :51-63 comment. New test: A(1-5) -> B(1-2) -> A, where spyCreate 'AuraMasterAnchor3' counts 0 on return and the container draws A's data (red under: dropping the destroyed instance). Regenerate docs/test-cases.md and the README badge. In-client smoke: same table address after the round trip, and no memory climb.
findings.verify_reason: In modules/ContainerManager.lua:107-108, CM.Sync's non-deferred branch calls inst:Destroy() and drops the instance. Destroy (modules/Container.lua:539-546) only hides frames and clears their points. The next follow() for that id (:85-93) finds no instance and no retiring entry, so it calls NS.Container.New(id). That runs CreateFrame('Frame','AuraMasterAnchor'..id, ...) again (Container.lua:43), leaking the old frame set and overwriting the global. Ids come back on a profile switch, copy or reset, which the comment at :51-63 itself acknowledges. The only reuse path is the deferred retiring table. Medium fits a real leak gated behind an uncommon action. The dormant-table remediation fits the existing revive/staleData design.

findings.title: UNIT_AURA registered via AceEvent for every unit while a 'without a duration' container exists; the standard's carve-out permits a player/pet unit-filtered frame
findings.evidence: events:RegisterEvent('UNIT_AURA', onUnitAura), where onUnitAura discards everything except player and pet. The header rationale ('vendored AceEvent has no RegisterUnitEvent') is stale: events-frames-taint-§1 now has a named carve-out that cites this addon. Offline, unitAuraOther costs 0.00013 ms/iter and 0 B. The client dispatch cost is unverified with no in-client capture. It is reachable only when a container sets durationMode to 'only without a duration'; no starter does. The audit ('checked and not filed') treats the AceEvent path as compliant and the carve-out as optional.
findings.remediation: Optional adoption of the events-frames-taint-§1 MAY carve-out. Hold one private frame on the module, TS.unitFrame = TS.unitFrame or CreateFrame('Frame'). Its single OnEvent dispatches to onUnitAura. syncAuraListen opens it with RegisterUnitEvent('UNIT_AURA','player','pet') and closes it with UnregisterEvent('UNIT_AURA'). TS.Stop must unregister it by hand, because AceEvent's UnregisterAllEvents does not reach it. Reuse the frame across disable/enable. Rewrite the :13-21 header: AceEvent still lacks RegisterUnitEvent, and this is the carve-out. Tests: the test_disabled census includes the frame, and test_timedspells asserts the frame's __unitEvents.UNIT_AURA == {'player','pet'} (the kit mock already records it at tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:226, so no mock work is needed). Replace the perf.lua unitAuraOther scenario, update docs/performance.md, and put pre/post in-client captures in docs/perf-analysis/ if the change is taken.
findings.verify_reason: The code matches the evidence. modules/TimedSpells.lua:121 registers UNIT_AURA through AceEvent, and onUnitAura (:111-113) keeps only player and pet. The events-frames-taint.md §1 carve-out does exist and cites this exact shape, but it is a MAY. The first bullet's MUST (use AceEvent) is what the addon does today, so this is an optional optimization, not a deviation. The header at :13-14 is only half stale. 'The vendored AceEvent has no RegisterUnitEvent' is still true, as the standard itself says. What is stale is 'never a private frame (events-frames-taint-§1)', which implies the frame is forbidden. The impact is unmeasured in the client, 0.00013 ms/iter offline, and reachable only when a container uses the non-starter 'only without a duration' mode, and registration is already gated out of combat and secrecy. That is Low, not Medium. The remediation matches the carve-out's MUSTs (held on the module, unregistered by hand in Stop, reused across cycles). The kit mock already records RegisterUnitEvent (tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:226), so the 'testkit gap' contingency does not apply.

findings.title: The host re-implements LibKa0s's tabbed-page render and page-banner chrome (Helpers.RenderTabbedPage, buildContainerHeader)
findings.locations: settings/OptionsSetup.lua:659 (RenderTabbedPage), :560 collectTabs, :583 settleActiveTab, :624 renderActiveTab, :480-504 buildContainerHeader (:484 raw Dropdown, :497 raw Button); libs/LibKa0s/OptionsWidgets.lua:3861 O.RenderTabbedSchema; libs/LibKa0s/OptionsTabs.lua:1029 O.PageBanner

findings.remediation: U-1 in LibKa0s: additive fields on O.RenderTabbedSchema (tabs rendered by a host callback and placed before a group; disabledFor(cfg) + disabledNotice; chrome(ctx) hook), and an optional right-half action button on O.PageBanner. Bump the OptionsWidgets and OptionsTabs minors by 1. Existing callers are unchanged. Evaluate it against anti-pattern #55 with the other candidate consumers first. U-2: re-vendor the WHOLE LibKa0s folder into every consumer as its own commit (diff -rq empty), with a revendor bundle. Then C-04b: replace RenderTabbedPage/buildContainerHeader with RenderTabbedSchema(..., {tabs, disabledFor, disabledNotice, chrome}) and PageBanner+action, re-pointing the test_optionssetup and test_pages_* tab cases. findings.verify_reason: The cited evidence is accurate. settings/OptionsSetup.lua:659 defines Helpers.RenderTabbedPage with its own chrome hook and disabledNotice, and buildContainerHeader at :480-504 builds a raw AceGUI Dropdown and Button. The library ships O.RenderTabbedSchema (libs/LibKa0s/OptionsWidgets.lua:3861, signature ctx, pageKey, afterGroup, pairWith, with no tabs/disabled/chrome fields) and O.PageBanner (OptionsTabs.lua:1029). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:821-829 has no deviation row for it. The routing is right: extend upstream additively, then re-vendor the whole folder, and never edit libs/ locally. The severity is inflated. This is a structural or duplication gap (anti-pattern #47 shape) with no user-reachable defect, and the AUDIT.md grade-by-impact table puts structural gaps at Low. It also has to clear anti-pattern #55 (per-consumer behavior flags) before promotion, which the remediation already notes.

findings.title: Event registration is bare sequential RegisterEvent calls, with no per-event pcall isolation and no record of rejected names
findings.evidence: RegisterLifecycleEvents makes eight bare self:RegisterEvent calls, ending with ADDON_RESTRICTION_STATE_CHANGED. TS.Sync registers three more, and syncAuraListen registers UNIT_AURA. An unknown name raises and takes the rest of the block with it. Every name is valid on 12.1, so this is latent.
findings.remediation: Upstream first: nominate a SafeRegisterEvent(target, event, handler, record) helper to LibKa0s-Core-1.0 (a C_EventUtils.IsEventValid front-gate plus pcall, appending refused names to a caller-owned list). Optionally, LibKa0s-DebugLog renders the rejected list inside [Init]. It clears library-stack-§7's promotion bars because every addon is bound by events-frames-taint-§1. If it ships, re-vendor the whole folder with a bundle. If declined, add a host NS.RegisterEventSafe in core/CoreSetup.lua. Route RegisterLifecycleEvents (as a loop over a module-level list), TS.Sync, syncAuraListen and the LifecycleSetup PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED hold through it. Record rejects in NS.RejectedEvents and surface them in the [Init] summary (optionally /am debug events). Test with kit M.__badEvents = {ADDON_RESTRICTION_STATE_CHANGED=true}: the other seven still register and the name is recorded (red under: bare RegisterEvent).
findings.rule_ref: events-frames-taint-§1 (an unknown event name raises; IsEventValid front-gate SHOULD)
findings.verify_reason: core/AuraMaster.lua:57-67 has eight bare self:RegisterEvent calls. modules/TimedSpells.lua:140-142 and :121 are bare too, and so is core/LifecycleSetup.lua:71 (addon:RegisterEvent(PENDING_EVENT, ...)). events-frames-taint.md §1 says that 'A registration block MUST survive one bad name ... every RegisterEvent goes through a single pcalled helper' and that rejected names MUST be recorded and reachable by the player. grep finds no IsEventValid, pcall or safe-register helper in core/, modules/, settings/ or the vendored libs/LibKa0s, nor in the LibKa0s repo. All the names are valid on the live client, so this is latent and Low is right, though it is a MUST failure. Upstream-first with a host fallback is the right routing, and the kit's M.__badEvents exists (tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:715-725) for the test.

findings.title: Degradation stubs copy library behavior; the Options stub composers rebuild composed blocks instead of answering an empty row list
findings.locations: settings/OptionsSetup.lua:175-280 (composeBlock, ColorPair, FontGroup, BorderGroup, BarGroup, MasterControls); tests/test_optionssetup.lua:369; settings/Slash.lua:388-391 (stub.DisabledLine); core/PoolSetup.lua:17-49; docs/settings-panel.md
findings.evidence: Each stub is described as 'spelled as the library spells it', which makes it the copy that drifts (anti-pattern #56). Since v2.64.0, stub composer members MUST answer an empty row list, and a host copy of a composed block inside the stub is anti-pattern #73. The test pins #NS2.Schema == #NS.Schema, when it should pin full, degraded and delta. The Slash stub re-spells the library refusal line. The Pool stub copies New/Acquire/ReleaseAll/Counts, which is defensible because a pool-less preview leaks. Only degraded installs reach any of this.
findings.remediation: Options stub (the audit's v2.64.0 ruling overrides the review's 'keep if validation fails' fallback): every composer answers {}, MasterControls answers {}, function() end, and composeBlock is deleted. Update the header comment to cite options-ui-§1. Replace the :369 assertion with three pins: the full-load count, the library-absent count, and the named composer delta (red under: a non-empty stub composer). Add a fall-together case: on the degraded load, /am set <composed path> answers the unavailable line. Make NS.ValidateSchema and the degraded path validation tolerate the smaller schema. Update docs/settings-panel.md 'The degraded panel'. Slash stub: keep DisabledLine but make it falsifiable with a test_surface_parity case comparing the with-library and without-library strings (red under: the library rewording). Pool stub: keep it, and tighten its comment to give the leak reason.
findings.verify_reason: settings/OptionsSetup.lua:175-280 holds composeBlock and composers that rebuild the ColorPair/FontGroup/BorderGroup/BarGroup/MasterControls leaf blocks. options-ui.md:53-58 says stub composers 'MUST answer an empty row list', that 'a host copy of a composed block inside the stub is anti-pattern #73', and that the suite MUST pin the full count, the library-absent count and the delta. tests/test_optionssetup.lua:369 instead asserts #NS2.Schema == #NS.Schema, the opposite pin. The Slash stub DisabledLine at settings/Slash.lua:388-391 re-spells the library string as described. Only degraded installs reach any of this, so Low is right. Anti-pattern #56 is about member-set drift rather than behavior copies, so #73 and options-ui-§1 are the load-bearing citations.

findings.title: CM.Init and CM.Announce build container frames while the addon is stood down, contradicting the doc comment
findings.evidence: CM.Init runs whatever the latch says. A player who logs in disabled, or switches profile while disabled, gets an anchor and a drag handle per container, left in CreateFrame's default shown state. They are empty and invisible. The comment says Init is called 'only when the addon is actually running'. The disabled suite covers only enabled->disabled.
findings.remediation: C-06: when NS.IsStoodDown(), CM.Init returns after EnsureAuraContainer + TimedSpells.Sync, and CM.Announce skips CM.Sync. LifecycleSetup standUp calls NS.ContainerManager.Sync() before ApplyVisibility. Fix the :568-569 doc. Test: log in disabled, spyCreate 'AuraMasterAnchor' counts 0; on enable the instances exist and draw (red under: CM.Init building before the latch check).
findings.verify_reason: core/AuraMaster.lua:51 calls CM.Init outside the `if not NS.IsStoodDown()` block. modules/ContainerManager.lua:570-579 gates only StartListening; CM.Sync (:92) still runs follow() -> NS.Container.New, which does CreateFrame('Frame','AuraMasterAnchor'..id) and builds a handle (modules/Container.lua:43-51). The doc at :568-569 says Init runs 'only when the addon is actually running', which is false. CM.Announce (:127-131) also syncs while down; rebuildProfile's comment (core/AuraMaster.lua:163-165) wrongly says CM.Init reads the latch. slash-commands-§7 says only the setup list 'comes up on load in either state', so feature frames built at a disabled login go against the spirit of the rule. Nothing draws, so low is right. The remediation is sound: standUp has to call Sync before ApplyVisibility, which it does not do today (core/LifecycleSetup.lua:108-120).

findings.title: Degraded Lifecycle stub is level-triggered (runs full standUp on every SyncEnabled), where the library is edge-triggered
findings.evidence: NS.SyncEnabled calls standDown or standUp on every call, including OnInitialize before PLAYER_LOGIN and every profile switch. standUp re-registers events, arms an apply timer and re-reparents the Blizzard frames, which means redundant apply passes. It affects only installs where libs/LibKa0s failed LibStub's floor.
findings.remediation: Keep a local `down = false` in the degraded branch. SyncEnabled computes want = not enabledStored() and calls standDown/standUp only when want ~= down, then sets down = want. Add the case to tests/test_lifecycle.lua (or whichever suite already loads tests/degraded_env.lua): two unchanged SyncEnabled calls arm one apply timer and register the lifecycle events once. Classify it as correctness (degraded-path parity), not a library-stack-§7 deviation.
findings.rule_ref: library-stack-§7 (the stub mirrors the member's contract)
findings.verify_reason: Real. core/LifecycleSetup.lua:128-130 calls standDown or standUp on every SyncEnabled. SyncEnabled runs from OnInitialize (core/AuraMaster.lua:32), from every profile callback (:160) and from the enabled row's onChange. standUp re-registers events and arms RequestApply. The path is reachable only when LibKa0s-Lifecycle is absent, so low. Two fixes. tests/degraded_env.lua is an environment builder, not a suite ('Not a suite (tests/run.lua does not list it)'), so the test belongs in a suite that loads it, such as tests/test_lifecycle.lua. And library-stack-§7 (:110) only says a setup file degrades to a stub. It does not say the stub must mirror the member's edge semantics, so the rule_ref is loose and this is a correctness defect, not a standards deviation. Start the local `down` at false, the library's empty-latch state, so the first SyncEnabled of an enabled load stays a no-op as it does with the library.

findings.title: The panel's Test mode checkbox is accepted while the addon is disabled, while /am test and the launcher refuse
findings.evidence: The row is bound straight to NS.Preview.SetTestMode. Ticking it while disabled silently sets NS.State.testMode = true, and the addon comes back up in test mode when enabled. The state is session-only, with no SavedVariables write.
findings.remediation: C-09: row.set refuses turning it on while NS.IsDisabled() and prints NS.Slash.DisabledLine() (one refusal line from the dispatcher). Turning it off stays allowed. Test in test_disabled.lua: a panel set while disabled leaves testMode false and prints one refusal line.
findings.verify_reason: settings/General.lua:107-113 binds row.set straight to NS.Preview.SetTestMode(v) with no disabled gate. modules/Preview.lua:28-40 refuses only in combat, so ticking the box while disabled sets NS.State.testMode = true and sends VISIBILITY_CHANGED. The library composer adds no gate either (libs/LibKa0s/OptionsCompose.lua:526-535: 'The host binds get/set'), so the fix is correctly routed to the host. The launcher refuses while disabled (core/LauncherSetup.lua:118-122), and `test` is not in liveVerbs (settings/Slash.lua:124-133), so the dispatcher refuses it. The panel row is the one inconsistent surface. It is session-only and nothing draws while stood down, so low. The remediation is correct.

findings.title: Two one-shot C_Timer.After callbacks armed before a stand-down cannot be canceled and wake up to find the latch
findings.locations: modules/ContainerManager.lua:155 (C_Timer.After(0, CM.FlushPending)); modules/ContainerManager.lua:253; modules/ContainerManager.lua:557-563 (CM.StopListening); modules/TimedSpells.lua:106 (C_Timer.After(0.5, scanTick)); modules/TimedSpells.lua:94-97; modules/TimedSpells.lua:131-134; modules/TimedSpells.lua:162-164
findings.evidence: FlushPending returns on NS.IsStoodDown() and scanTick drops on its listening guard. The file's own comment admits C_Timer.After returns no handle to cancel. The standard says timers must not be 'left armed to wake up and find a flag'. Graded Low: each wakes at most once and never re-arms.
findings.remediation: Switch both to C_Timer.NewTimer handles: flushTimer = NewTimer(0, fn) and scanTimer = NewTimer(0.5, scanTick). Cancel them in CM.StopListening and TS.Stop, and reset the scheduled and scanScheduled flags on cancel so the stand-up's RequestApply(nil, true) is not swallowed. Keep the listening guard as defence in depth and rewrite the :162-164 comment. Confirm the kit mock's C_Timer.NewTimer handle :Cancel() removes it from __timers(); if it does not, that is an upstream testkit item. Test: test_disabled step 4 arms both before disabling and asserts __timers() is empty (red under: C_Timer.After). Step 9 re-enable still passes.
findings.verify_reason: modules/ContainerManager.lua:155 arms C_Timer.After(0, CM.FlushPending) with no handle. :253 FlushPending returns on NS.IsStoodDown(). CM.StopListening (:557-563) resets the queue but cancels nothing and leaves `scheduled` alone. modules/TimedSpells.lua:106 arms C_Timer.After(0.5, scanTick). scanTick (:94-97) drops on the `listening` guard, TS.Stop (:131-134) cancels nothing, and the TS.StandDown comment (:162-164) admits the timer is dropped by the guard rather than canceled. slash-commands.md:190 says every timer is canceled, 'not left armed to wake up and find a flag'. Each timer fires at most once and never re-arms, so low is right. The kit supports the fix: tests/_kit/mock_record.lua:77-84 says NewTimer's Cancel has been real since revision 17, and __timers() returns the live set. The remediation's point about resetting scheduled/scanScheduled on cancel is needed so the stand-up's RequestApply is not swallowed.

findings.title: tests/page_helpers.lua has a stray bare CR at :80, so git classifies it binary and it escapes normalization
findings.evidence: Line 80 ends \r\r\n. git ls-files --eol shows i/-text, and the blob is stored CRLF (272 CR). The E-8 working-tree one-liner counts 1 file. The kit's test_eol is green over it (the known lone-CR limit).
findings.remediation: Delete the stray \r, run git add --renormalize tests/page_helpers.lua, and confirm i/lf w/crlf. The (e) one-liner should print 0. Upstream testkit hardening is tracked separately in AuraMaster-A-18.
findings.verify_reason: `git ls-files --eol tests/page_helpers.lua` gives `i/-text w/-text attr/text=auto eol=crlf`. Line 80 ends `\r\r\n` (checked with od). The index blob holds 272 CRs over 271 lines, and the working tree has 271 CR. The first of the two CRs on line 80 is a lone CR, and git's text=auto check treats a lone CR as binary, which is why this file escaped normalization. tests/_kit/test_eol.lua:175-185 counts only LFs that follow a CR, so it stays green over this file. line-endings.md:505-510 names the lone CR as the one-liner's known limit and still says 'No file in the collection has one'. The line-endings §7 text 'clear a red by re-checkout, never renormalize' is not violated: that text assumes the index is already correct, and here the index itself is wrong. So `--renormalize` on this one path (it skips git's CRLF-already-in-index guard) is the right fix.

findings.title: LibKa0s testkit test_eol misses a tracked file git classifies -text under text=auto (the lone-CR blind spot)
findings.locations: LibKa0s testkit test_eol (vendored as tests/_kit/); AuraMaster tests/page_helpers.lua:80 as the example
findings.evidence: test_eol stays green over tests/page_helpers.lua even though git stores it unnormalized as i/-text. line-endings-§7 names the lone-CR case as the one-liner's known limit.
findings.remediation: In LibKa0s, extend tests/_kit/test_eol.lua. For every tracked path with text not unset and no NUL byte (the same set the gate already scans), also count lone CRs: a byte 13 that is not followed by byte 10. Fail with the path and the line number whenever that count is above 0. Do not key the check on the index's -text classification alone, because that would redden real auto-detected binaries such as PanelMaster's realesrgan binary. Add a fixture test for a `\r\r\n` line. Update line-endings-§7's lone-CR note in WowAddonStandards: the kit now catches the case, and 'No file in the collection has one' is no longer true. Tag LibKa0s and re-vendor the whole of LibKa0s (libs/LibKa0s/ and tests/_kit/) into every addon. Land the local AM-30 fix first, so that AuraMaster is green when the new case arrives.
findings.verify_reason: The blind spot is real. The terminators() function in tests/_kit/test_eol.lua:175-185 counts only LF bytes and whether a CR comes before each one, so a lone CR inside a line (tests/page_helpers.lua:80) passes. The upstream routing (LibKa0s testkit, then re-vendor) is correct. The proposed check is wrong, though. Failing whenever a path's index classification is -text under text=auto would also fail every real binary git auto-detected without an explicit binary marking. The kit's own comment at :199 cites PanelMaster's extension-less tools/artwork/bin/realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan, and that file would go red across the collection. The gate should look for the lone CR directly. line-endings.md:505-510 should also be amended, since its 'No file in the collection has one' is now false.

findings.title: AUDIT.md contradicts itself: step 4 hard-codes High for an unrecorded re-vendor tag, while step 5's impact table grades docs-only gaps Low
findings.locations: WowAddonStandards AUDIT.md step 4 (re-vendor check) vs step 5 (impact table)
findings.evidence: The auditor had to record both grades on AM-21 (High by step 4, Low by step 5) 'so the tension inside the playbook stays visible'.
findings.remediation: In WowAddonStandards, reconcile the playbook: either have step 4 defer to step 5's impact grading, or state explicitly that step 4's grade overrides step 5.
findings.verify_reason: Checked WowAddonStandards/AUDIT.md. In step 4 (re-vendor bundle check), lines 341-342 say 'A tag vendored with no bundle naming it and no ## Documented deviations row saying why is a **High** finding', and line 335 repeats the High. Step 5's impact table (lines 863-873) says 'A doc-only or config-only failure is Low or Info even when the rule it fails is a MUST'. It also defines High as something a user, their SavedVariables or their session can hit today. A missing re-vendor bundle is a docs-only gap, so the two passages give contradictory grades. Neither passage says which one takes precedence. This is a real playbook tension, correctly routed upstream, at info.

findings.title: The v1.55.0 revendor bundle took its delta base from the library's previous tag (v1.54.2), not from the addon's actually vendored tag (v1.53.0)
findings.locations: docs/revendor/2026-09-23-v1.55.0/01_DELTA.md:1-15 (produced by /wow-addon:revendor-libka0s steps 2-4, run non-interactively by the suite standards sweep)
findings.evidence: 01_DELTA.md runs 'git -C ../LibKa0s log --oneline v1.54.2..v1.55.0', but the repo's previous re-vendor commit f6f61d3 was v1.53.0. Inferred from the bundle text: the base was not derived from the addon's CLAUDE.md provenance line or its last vendoring commit. Other addons re-vendored by the same sweep may share the error.
findings.remediation: In the wow-addon plugin's revendor-libka0s command (and any sweep script that drives it), derive the delta base from the addon's recorded vendored tag (CLAUDE.md provenance or last libs/LibKa0s commit), not the library's previous tag. Before the collection-wide LibKa0s re-vendor in this plan, check the other addons' v1.55.0 bundles for the same misstatement.
findings.rule_ref: audit-review-history (a re-vendor commit implies a bundle)
findings.verify_reason: AuraMaster/docs/revendor/2026-09-23-v1.55.0/01_DELTA.md:1 is headed 'Delta: LibKa0s v1.54.2 -> v1.55.0' and runs `git log v1.54.2..v1.55.0` and `diff --stat v1.54.2 v1.55.0`. `git log -- libs/LibKa0s` shows the previous re-vendor is f6f61d3 'Re-vendor LibKa0s v1.53.0', directly before f6f3ffb 'Re-vendor LibKa0s v1.55.0'. The bundle therefore leaves out the v1.54.x span that AuraMaster actually received. This is a documentation-accuracy defect in a frozen record and no user can reach it, so Low is right. The root cause is in how the command or the sweep driving it picked the base, so routing to wow-addon is right. The remediation already covers both the command and the sweep script and adds a cross-addon check. The misstated bundle is frozen and must not be edited, so any correction belongs in the next bundle or a note.
